title.en: The Cold War, Marshall Plan and the Chinese Revolution
Two giants and one divided world

text.en: After 1945 two super powers, the USA and the USSR, faced each other without a direct war, and the world split into two blocs. At the same time the old empires were fading and, in China, a revolution changed the largest country in Asia.

The Second World War ended the era of European colonial empires and left the USA and the USSR as the two super powers, dividing the world into antagonistic blocs.
This tension without direct war between the blocs is the Cold War, which triggered conflicts in Korea, Cuba, Vietnam and West Asia and ended with the fall of the Berlin Wall.
Under the Marshall Plan the USA helped rebuild war-ravaged Europe, while the USSR won goodwill by supporting liberation struggles in Asia and Africa.
The Non-Aligned Movement played a limited role in containing the conflict between the two power blocs.
In China the Manchu dynasty had ruled since about 1650; peasants suffered high rents and the Opium Wars forced China to open its ports to western powers.
Discontent led to uprisings like the Taiping Rebellion (1850-64); in 1911 the army mutinied, the Manchu rule fell and Dr Sun Yat-sen became provisional president of the new Republic.
The Second World War helped bring the communist revolution in China, after which the People's Republic was proclaimed in 1949 under Mao Zedong.

problem.en: A weak ruler, poor peasants and foreign powers controlling ports: what kind of situation produces a revolution?

text.en: Poverty and high rents anger the peasants.
A new leader or party offers change, as Sun Yat-sen and later the Communists did.

prompt.en: What was the Cold War and what was the Marshall Plan?

requiredIdeas.en: Rivalry of USA and USSR without direct war

commonMisconceptions.en: Saying the Cold War was fought directly between the two powers

points.en: After 1945: USA and USSR as two super powers.
Cold War: rivalry without a direct war; ended with fall of the Berlin Wall.
Marshall Plan: US aid to rebuild Europe.
China: Manchu rule ended in 1911; People's Republic in 1949.
